answer: Each agent identity must post a non-transferable bond into a permissioned kernel registry that signs only one claim per human sponsor. A second alias under the same sponsor is refused, so a Sybil run needs N funded sponsors, not N free keys. Every claim emits an on-chain echo of the sponsor and stake, making duplicates publicly attributable, and a rejected alias leaves a permanent sable mark that blocks refunds. Bonds stay locked for the whole challenge window, so an attacker must lock N bonds for weeks and risk losing all of them to audit. That makes mass duplication unprofitable.
